gaps.sentence: The castle ___ (restore) at present, so the east wing is closed to visitors.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive: is being + restored for work in progress now.

gaps.sentence: The suspect is believed ___ the country weeks ago.
gaps.explanation: Believe + to-infinitive; 'weeks ago' demands the perfect infinitive to have left.

gaps.sentence: Nothing ___ about the leak until the inspector came.
gaps.explanation: 'Nothing was said' — the passive of 'nobody said'.

gaps.sentence: The temple is thought ___ (build) more than two thousand years ago.
gaps.explanation: Perfect passive infinitive: to have been + built for an event earlier than the main verb.

gaps.sentence: The village ___ (reach) by road until 1962; only mules could make the climb.
gaps.explanation: 'Until 1962' describes a past state of affairs: could not be + past participle.

gaps.sentence: The results ___ (EXPECT) to be announced later today.
gaps.explanation: 'Later today' requires the present: are expected to be announced.

gaps.sentence: The museum ___ (close) to the public on Mondays.
gaps.explanation: Present simple passive: is + closed. No agent needed; the routine is what matters.

gaps.sentence: The suspect ___ to have left the country.
